title: Inference on Causal Effects in Mixed-Noise Linear Models under a Known Partial Order
banked_reason: Stage 0.5: tier=subfield < floor=field; paper-score ceiling 7.2 < 7.4 and not salvageable in scope.
gap_reasons: The note proves matched logarithmic covariance and whole-fiber Hausdorff rates only on the fixed three-variable exponent-two subclass; over the broader Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi class it proves lower bounds alone.

The causal interpretation remains confined to laws satisfying the explicit greatest-Gaussian-divisor condition and known raywise Fourier envelopes and exponents, so this is not general mixed-noise inference.
The motivating pcalg and yeast workflow is not implemented or empirically demonstrated, which limits the significance case for a leading econometrics journal.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved the finite-sample Fourier covariance region, whole-fiber coverage and logarithmic upper rate, the explicit smooth-splice lower pair, its transfer to a published mixed-noise class, and the literal-Laplace root-N boundary. A validity-gate repair restamped all five affected proofs, resolved the smooth-splice OEQ, synchronized the rendered note, and left a clean graph with a passing math review. The result remains below the field floor because matched rates hold only on the fixed three-variable subclass and the wider-class and consumer claims are limited to lower-only transfer and an unimplemented application.
tldr: Under mutually independent, unit-variance, nonconstant Gaussian-indecomposable latent sources, a full-column-rank identified loading convention, and an explicit greatest-Gaussian-divisor condition, a known partial order leaves a finite Cholesky-effect fiber. The note represents that fiber by treatment-predecessor ideals and maps a measurable finite-sample characteristic-function covariance region into simultaneous coverage of every compatible effect, including exact collisions. Expected covariance and Hausdorff errors are of order \(1/\log N\) on the fixed ordinary-smooth Fourier class. An explicit positive smooth Laplace--Student splice attains matching covariance, singleton-effect, and honest-diameter lower bounds there; because this fixed class is contained in the Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi Assumptions 2--4 class, the three lower bounds also transfer to that published class and to every superclass containing the fixed splice class. No logarithmic upper bound is claimed for the broader published class. Literal standardized-Laplace sources form a root-\(N\) fourth-cumulant boundary.
gap: Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi give finite population identification for mixed-noise models, while Wang--Kolar--Drton's Algorithm 3 and Lemma 1 propagate an asymptotic confidence set for an identifiable additive-error ordering into coverage of one total effect. Neither gives a finite-sample event covering every partial-order-compatible effect after greatest-Gaussian-divisor recovery under latent common sources; the two law classes are nonnested, and the moment-compatible collision lower pair remains open.
fill: The project supplies the predecessor-ideal functional, an explicit centered ray region with clipping and fallback, a theorem-level nonnesting comparison and finite-sample simultaneous whole-fiber guarantee, a conditional route to the fixed-class logarithmic converse, and a literal-Laplace boundary controlled by a global Lipschitz modulus.
